title: Bertini–Noether over a fraction field
statement: Let A be a commutative domain, F a fraction field of A, and E an algebraically closed field with an F-algebra structure. Let n be a natural number and P in A[X_1,...,X_n] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. If the coefficient image of P under A -> F -> E is irreducible, there is a nonzero a in A such that every map phi from A to any field k with phi(a) nonzero sends P to an irreducible polynomial of the same total degree.

proof.text: Use the proved source-library theorem MvPolynomial.bertini_noether. Its coefficient algebra parametrizes products of two polynomials each of total degree less than d = totalDegree P. Chevalley makes the image of its spectrum constructible. If this image contained the generic point of Spec A, localizing a prime above that point and passing to a maximal ideal would give a finite extension of F, by the weak Nullstellensatz. Embed that extension into E. The resulting coefficient point factors P into two factors of degrees less than d, contradicting irreducibility and additivity of total degree. A constructible set missing the generic point is contained in V(a0) for some nonzero a0. Choose a nonzero coefficient c in total degree d and put a = a0*c. At any field specialization not killing a, c survives, so total degree remains d and is positive. A factorization with both factors nonunits has two positive degrees strictly below d, hence gives a point of the coefficient algebra and puts the specialization kernel in its constructible image. It must then kill a0, a contradiction. Thus the specialization is irreducible and has degree d. If n = 0 the irreducibility hypothesis is impossible. This entire argument is already proved in the cited source module, with no sorry.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0557; proved Chevalley coefficient-algebra argument in WeilConjectures.RingTheory.BertiniNoether
